reasons: Reproduced the instance: the variant compiles, testMath280 fails with 'final a value=0, final b value=2, f(a)=-0.477, f(b)=0', and the full variant suite fails ONLY testMath280. (a) Only the gold sees function values and makes the return-or-throw decision. On the trigger, its first pass gives a=0, b=2 with f(2)=0, so the loop stops (f(a)*f(b) is not > 0). It then throws 'no bracketing interval is found' although [0,2] brackets the root by the convention of the facade and the solvers. The facade, hops 1-4 and the callers only propagate that exception; none has logic of its own that breaks its contract. (b) Every hop's javadoc matches its code: hop 2 checks maximumIterations, hop 3 checks initial and the bounds, and hops 1 and 4 are pure pass-throughs. No hop's documentation leaves room for it to own a zero-product decision it never sees. (c) No competing repair. Argument edits at hops cannot pass the trigger. The trigger needs a bracket with an endpoint exactly at 2 (Brent on any other bracket misses the 1e-12 tolerance, probed), and every such bracket has a zero product that the gold rejects. Two passing hop-4 edits exist; both are bypasses or violate the documentation. A zero to 1e-300 function wrapper breaks the facade's documented loop termination ({0,3} instead of {0,2}). A catch of ConvergenceException that rebuilds {a,b} from its message arguments re-implements the gold's decision and leaves the gold violating its own contract. Both pass the full suite and are recorded. (d) The hop and gold names (enclosingInterval, rootInterval, intervalAround, searchInterval, expandInterval) are neutral, and no added comment marks the fault. The lie (the step 'is doubled after every pass ... grows geometrically') is about step size and names neither the zero-product case nor any hop. (e) The gold is the fifth call below the facade. The hops are in five distinct existing classes (BlockFieldMatrix, MathUtils, BlockRealMatrix, BigMatrixImpl, EigenDecompositionImpl). The facade body is the null guard plus one call. One added procedural sentence describes doubling that the code does not do. The gold's javadoc ('until it brackets a root'; 'ConvergenceException if no bracketing interval is found') is silent on zero endpoints. The trigger is an existing test and is the only new failure (confirmed by my own full run). The only difference between correct.patch and variant.patch is the gold's 3-line return. (f) The convention that a zero endpoint completes the bracket is pinned outside the gold by several sources: the facade's pristine javadoc ('f(a) * f(b) <= 0 -- success!'); BrentSolver.solve(f,min,max) ('either min or max is a root' when yMin*yMax == 0); RiddersSolver.solve ('check for zeros before verifying bracketing'); BisectionSolver.solve (keeps [min,m] when fm*fmin is not positive); and BrentSolverTest::testRootEndpoints ('endpoint is root'), which passes on the variant.
notes: 1) Inaccurate spec claim: ownership_reason says that after the exception 'the interval is lost'. In fact ConvergenceException.getArguments() carries a, b, f(a) and f(b), so a hop can recover the interval (bypass row 2). This does not change ownership, because the recovery re-implements the gold's decision while the gold still breaks its own contract. 2) The pristine 4-arg bracket overload, which sits on the trigger path, documents a strict 'f(a) * f(b) < 0' success condition, while the 5-arg facade documents '<= 0'. Under the strict reading the defect would be the gold's loop guard rather than its post-loop check, but it stays inside the gold. The trigger's 1e-12 tolerance needs the {0,2} bracket, i.e. the non-strict convention. 3) For the trace checker, not counted as leakage here: in the variant gold the loop guard stops on f(a)*f(b) <= 0 while the post-loop check throws on >= 0, so the two conditions disagree on the zero case. This is the shape of the original Math-85 defect. 4) The lie is appended after the last @throws tag without a leading '*', so rendered javadoc attaches it to the @throws IllegalArgumentException description. It contradicts the pristine 'by one unit each time' sentence, as the recipe intends. 5) Ownership tests UnivariateRealSolverUtilsTest::testBracketSin, GammaDistributionTest::testValues and TDistributionTest::testSmallDf do not exercise a zero endpoint. They guard ordinary bracketing, so the zero-endpoint pin rests on the facade javadoc, the solver code and BrentSolverTest::testRootEndpoints. 6) Probe classes and edits lived only in /private/tmp/mxb-xQTG58, which has been deleted.
